issues.legal_issue: Direct proof of monetary consideration is not invariably required to establish subletting when a tenant has given another person exclusive possession of the premises.
material_facts: The landlord sought eviction on the ground of subletting.
The Rent Controller and the Rent Control Appellate Tribunal found that the tenant had sublet the premises, and the High Court did not interfere with that finding.
The tenant challenged the finding on the ground that there was no positive finding or direct proof that the alleged sub-tenants paid consideration.
issues.conclusion: The Court held that consideration may be inferred from proved facts, including delivery of exclusive possession, and dismissed the challenge to the concurrent finding of subletting.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 14(1)(b) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, subletting involves the tenant giving up possession of the premises, wholly or in part, and putting another person in exclusive possession. Although payment of rent or monetary consideration is an essential element and may be paid, promised, or provided in cash or kind, it need not invariably be proved by affirmative direct evidence because such arrangements may be clandestine. A court may infer consideration from the facts proved, including exclusive possession. The Court relied on Rajbir Kaur v. S. Chokesiri & Co. (1989) 1 SCC 19 and distinguished Delhi Stationers & Printers v. Rajendra Kumar (1990) 2 SCC 331, Jagan Nath v. Chander Bhan (1988) 3 SCC 57, Smt. Krishnavati v. Hans Raj (1974) 1 SCC 289, Gopal Saran v. Satyanarayana (1989) 3 SCC 56, and United Bank of India v. Cooks and Kelvey Properties (P) Ltd. (1994) 5 SCC 9. United Bank did not establish that direct proof of consideration is required in every case; its result rested on facts showing retained control and constructive possession.

rule.if: challenge_to_eviction_for_subletting and tenant_parted_with_possession and another_person_in_exclusive_possession and direct_consideration_proof_absent and lower_courts_found_subletting

predicates.challenge_to_eviction_for_subletting: The proceeding challenges an eviction decision made on the ground that the tenant sublet the premises.
predicates.tenant_parted_with_possession: The tenant gave up possession of all or part of the premises to another person.
predicates.another_person_in_exclusive_possession: A person other than the tenant was in exclusive possession of the premises or part of them.
predicates.direct_consideration_proof_absent: The landlord did not establish payment of consideration through direct affirmative evidence.
predicates.lower_courts_found_subletting: The lower courts found that the tenant had sublet the premises.

issues.definition: When an eviction challenge concerns subletting, the tenant has parted with possession, another person has exclusive possession, direct proof of consideration is absent, and the lower courts found subletting, the finding may be sustained without direct proof of consideration.
